summary:
DAQQA (Arabic: دِقَّة — meaning Precision, Accuracy, and Heartbeat) is an integrated astronaut healthcare ecosystem designed to address the challenges of monitoring human physiology during long-duration spaceflight.

During deep space missions (such as lunar far-side sorties or Mars transit), continuous telemetry to Earth is impossible due to communication blackouts (Loss of Signal / LOS) and interplanetary transit latencies. DAQQA operates autonomously on the astronaut's wrist via Garmin smartwatches (Connect IQ / Monkey C), providing real-time physiological vigilance and haptic alarming, before syncing via a Dual-Export Architecture to NASA archives once ground network connectivity is re-established.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

DAQQA (Arabic: "precision, accuracy, heartbeat") is a prototype health monitoring system for astronauts on long-duration missions such as Artemis and Mars transit. During communication blackouts and transit delays, Earth cannot monitor an astronaut in real time, so DAQQA works on the astronaut's wrist without any ground connection.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Continuous biometrics: heart rate, heart rate variability (RMSSD), blood oxygen (SpO2), a stress index (1-100) and a muscle fatigue index (0-100). The two indices are simple estimates, not clinical measurements.

2. Behavioral check-ins: short sleep-quality and mood/stress questionnaires (scored 1-5) on the watch screen, timestamped alongside live sensor data.

3. Blackout operation: during a loss of signal, readings and survey answers are stored on the device. Thresholds (for example SpO2 below 90% or acute tachycardia) trigger a vibration and on-screen warning with no Earth connection needed.

4. Dual export: when ground contact returns, the stored data is split into two streams modeled on NASA's LSDA and LSAH programs: a de-identified research stream (anonymized IDs, 30-minute epochs, JSON/CSV) and an identified medical stream (AES-256-GCM encrypted with a SHA-256 integrity digest, FHIR/JSON for flight surgeons).

A mission-control web dashboard lets a flight surgeon view the data and test five scenarios: nominal routine, spacewalk exertion, communication blackout, acute hypoxia, and circadian desync with fatigue.

The watch app is written in Monkey C for Garmin Connect IQ devices.

BENEFITS

Astronauts get immediate on-wrist alerts when contact with Earth is impossible, and researchers and flight surgeons receive properly separated data once contact returns, protecting astronaut privacy.

GOALS

Support astronaut self-monitoring on future deep space missions. Next steps are personal baselines for each astronaut, radiation dose tracking, and validation against real analog-mission data.

LIMITATIONS

All data in this demo is simulated. DAQQA is decision support, not a diagnostic tool or medical device.

TOOLS

React 18, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons, HTML canvas (dashboard); Garmin Connect IQ and Monkey C (watch; targeting devices such as tactix 7, fenix 7 and descent Mk3); AES-256-GCM and SHA-256 (export security demo).
